# Analysis plan for pairwise ACT outcome fusion

## Data and split

This is a retrospective secondary analysis of the already scored [ACT rule-transfer benchmark](../confirmatory/protocol.md). Freeze this plan locally before scoring any new model. The earlier aggregate findings were known. The reuse of this evaluation set precludes a new independent confirmation.

Use the exact approved-rule training inventory and proposed-rule test inventory of the previous evaluator. Verify the public [W3C snapshot](https://github.com/w3c/wcag-act-rules/tree/4ce3d61b6f7b04cbf2df0082a3446e97248b9124) archive SHA-256 `d9f88266ad0a6664b76169ed9d19583441cbaad75629d87ea4e8d115d08898ad`. Verify the [source evaluator](../confirmatory/evaluate.py) SHA-256 `54d1e0d2d99d058579c4afe427724f5f0982efc05db228b4cb1b11be78110553` and the [released predictions](../confirmatory/predictions.csv) SHA-256 `358c30b1035f919d295a1c895f12ac395e1f1a8c8faee4b1cd7767cbf3324d31`. Check disjoint rule IDs, testcase IDs and normalized content hashes across model training and testing. Retain the previous overlap exclusions with the earlier four-tool study. Validate the held-out row keys, expected labels, and every report and baseline prediction against the earlier release before fitting the new models. Use only the public archive and the earlier release. Reserved data have no role in this analysis.

## Models and controls

The question is whether interactions between two exercised engine outcomes improve exact label prediction on rules held out from fitting. For example, a review request might change how to interpret a pass from another engine. Preserve the exact same 11 automated/linter report columns, collapse publisher procedure outcomes with the existing precedence and fit once on approved rules. Rule IDs, case metadata and text, and rule-level outcome aggregates stay out of the features. Train on all approved training cases with the original equal-rule weights scaled to mean one. Each new model is multinomial L2 logistic regression with an intercept, default L-BFGS solver, C=1, tolerance 1e-9, and at most 2,000 iterations. Use binary features without rescaling. Apply the original all-untested abstention to every logistic model. Break model score ties in the frozen label order failed, passed, inapplicable.

- **Additive control.** The prior logistic stack, with five indicators per engine, must reproduce the released predictions. This holds the inputs, main effects, weights and learner fixed.
- **Primary paired-outcome model.** Add a categorical interaction for each unordered engine pair. Each pair can activate one of 16 binary indicators when both engines are exercised. Exercised means anything other than untested, including cantTell. Every pair with at least one untested engine activates zero interaction indicators.
- **Missingness interaction control.** Keep the additive features and add only the nine remaining pair indicators where one or both engines are untested. This tests a different mechanism at identical data and model settings. It is a mechanism check with a different feature count.
- **Full interaction diagnostic.** Keep all 25 pair indicators to measure the combined effect. The diagnostics do not select a replacement primary model.

Use as contextual comparisons every frozen automated engine/linter and voting, fallback and naive Bayes baseline from the prior study. The two primary contrasts are against the additive control and smoothed confusion-matrix naive Bayes, identified in the prior study as its strongest competing ensemble by equal-rule exact accuracy.

## Endpoints and uncertainty

The primary endpoint is exact failed/passed/inapplicable accuracy averaged equally across all held-out rules. Abstention and review get zero credit. Publish each comparator's exact count, micro and equal-rule accuracy, failure detection, false alerts, abstentions and per-rule scores. For the primary contrasts report paired rule wins/ties/losses and the accuracy differences. Archive the aligned predictions on the complete inventory. Report descriptive scores on the rows with zero, one or at least two exercised panel members, the rows with conflicting decisive labels, and the original four-tool common support. Each slice macro-averages over rules represented in that slice.

For paired uncertainty, link held-out rules sharing a testcase ID or normalized content hash. Take the transitive connected components and use them as bootstrap blocks, including singleton rules. Draw the observed number of components with replacement, keep each component intact and re-average the sampled rules equally within each draw. Use 50,000 PCG64 draws with seed 42014, shared across contrasts. Use percentile intervals with linear quantiles. Record ordinary paired rule-block bootstrap intervals as a sensitivity using a separate PCG64 stream with seed 42015. The two primary contrasts each use two-sided 97.5% intervals for nominal 95% simultaneous coverage by Bonferroni. Call the result a retrospective improvement only if the component-bootstrap lower bound exceeds zero against both primary comparators. Report outcomes as observed if the gate fails. These intervals summarize sensitivity to benchmark rule composition with the fitted models held fixed. Rule grouping may miss semantic dependence and the benchmark has no probability sample of deployed pages or ACT rules.
